review_scope: 469 actually viewed all23-method contact-sheet overviews;25 preplanned and2 posthoc native label sheets actually viewed. Exported native overlays are not counted as inspected.
provisional_findings: B23, a diagnostic control outside the selectable candidate roster, has higher current-cohort mean IoU and runtime-adjusted utility than every selectable method. No claim of outperforming the best control is supported.

P11 leads selectable utility but visibly leaks onto exterior glass in multiple cases. Native TIGER11 inspection shows its triangular hole lies within actual white internal lumen included in the cyan reference semantic region, not demonstrated removal of visible tissue. TIGER28 fat-space holes likewise need semantic-support interpretation. It is not an anatomically validated background solution.

B23/P10/P12 recover reference-positive adipocyte spaces but also fill large exterior glass polygons or rectangles in BEETLE03/08 and GleasonXAI04. P10 additionally creates triangular glass spikes. P11 usually leaks less in these cases but still fails.

The unchanged white rule requires every RGB channel above 0.90 and saturation below 0.12. Sampled CAM glass is darker; all nonwhite pixels are protected by current native support contracts. BACKGROUND_PHOTOMETRY.json documents three posthoc visible-background rectangles, not independent glass ground truth or a cohort accuracy metric.

P03 stain-component regions frequently collapse broad tissue compartments to nuclear-scale speckle or an incorrect dominant class. Uniform centres in some cases do not disprove its observed failures elsewhere.

Fine reference septa, gland separations, small disconnected islands and rare classes remain poorly recovered by most appearance variants. Where a class is absent from the coarse input, all current closed-class variants miss it; those positive classes stay in the scoring denominator.

Reference-zero areas can be glass, lumen or visible unannotated tissue. All visible tissue is inferred; GT0 alone is not evidence of false foreground. PESO/OCELOT broad negative scoring adapters remain declared and saved masks are unchanged.

BCSS75 is a severe shared semantic failure: dense red upper islands and the purple lower network largely disappear into a broad green mask across methods. Background support changes do not resolve this.

BCSS80 makes native-support differences visible: B23 fills a pale lower-left exterior strip, P10 partially fills it with angular geometry, P11 removes most of it, and P12 cuts farther into image edges. BCSS71/76 also show P12 removing pale structures or borders.

Across the newly reviewed BCSS fields, actual internal white clefts and lumens are often filled by every variant; thin septa, small islands and absent-coarse classes remain missed. P15 sometimes extends a true rare-class branch but often adds false coloured rims and islands.

All 132 BCSS, 80 TIGER and 40 OCELOT overviews are now reviewed. BCSS108/114 internal white clefts are filled across methods; TIGER52 converted RGB mottling fragments broad compartments; TIGER47/53/57/60/79/80 native support restores pale adipose coverage but gland topology remains fused.

TIGER71 posthoc native crop exposes apparently empty exterior glass labelled stroma in the original source mask. Reproducible diagnostic verifies raw RGB/native RGB and raw mask/compacted native reference pixelwise identities. Selected 160 x 160 pixel rectangle is 100% reference class 2, median RGB 255 in every channel. Frozen scores reward filling it. This is a selected diagnostic, not independent glass annotation or a new cohort metric.

Native TIGER11 posthoc review corrects overview-only tissue-destruction suspicion: the P11 hole removes a visibly empty intratissue lumen included in the in-situ tumour semantic annotation. Exterior glass, adipocyte space and ductal lumens cannot be treated as one white-pixel category.

OCELOT23/29 particularly expose large score gains when native-support variants colour pale grey exterior glass green broad negative. The declared white-only zero-to-negative scoring adapter does not excuse anatomical exterior filling. Frozen scores are unchanged; native-support gains must not all be described as recovered tissue.

OCELOT21/31 show major merging of separate gland rings/walls and loss of lumens across most methods despite high broad-class scores. P03 destroys compartments and P15 often invents rare-class islands. OCELOT38 correctly demonstrates inference on real visible tissue in large reference-zero unscored regions.

All40 IGNITE overviews are reviewed. IGNITE33 exposes interior class competition: a lower reference-green network becomes blue with J01/M04/N10 and native-support children, while B22/C17/N08/P07/P08/P13/P14 suppress that blue; support alone cannot correct this. IGNITE25 converted RGB mottling fragments broad regions, and IGNITE32 has a false yellow rim around a green oval. Fine papillary structures and absent-coarse classes remain poorly recovered.

PESO05–08 actual overviews distinguish epithelial red walls from the broad negative green target, which is not expert stroma. Common support excludes large white gland lumens; B23/P10/P12 usually fill them green and P11 retains smaller holes. Broad wall recovery can coexist with merged fine fingers, added red filaments and distorted gland topology; P03 fragments the walls and P15 often thickens rims.

PESO12/19/24/26/38 show native support colouring clear glass or interfragment spaces green. PESO26 common support has sparse debris, whereas P11 expands it into solid green. P15 partially recovers fine epithelial linings in PESO18/38 but fails consistently enough elsewhere to reject.

GCSS32 shows simpler B22/C17 avoiding some purple-wing fragmentation introduced by field variants; GCSS20 retains an incorrect mottled red/green region across variants. GCSS18 absent-coarse grey islands are missed by all. P15 makes false yellow/grey/purple expansions in GCSS24/30/37.

All40 PUMA overviews are reviewed. Reference coverage is central-window only; outside visible tissue is inferred but unscored. Blue vessels absent from coarse labels remain missed across methods, while PUMA40 preserves blue when coarse provides it. PUMA27 merges red nests across thin green septa. PUMA11 native support fills upper glass grey; PUMA20 labels large clear lumens green across implementations.

All40 GleasonXAI overviews are reviewed. Broad sparse polygons can cover actual white tears, lumens and glass; native support gains therefore cannot be interpreted purely as recovered tissue. GleasonXAI11/12/29/35/40 show this conflict especially clearly. P10 produces spikes; P12 produces rounded rectangular foreground blankets; P11 often leaks less but still fails.

The five survivors are an explicit accuracy/runtime/visual/model-diversity choice, not the five highest utility ranks. P11 is mandatory candidate leader but B23 control remains higher. P10/P12 are rejected despite high utility for false glass geometries. C17 is retained as the fastest distinct palette branch despite lower utility than P02/P09.
next_action: Design15 distinct mathematical children, three per signed cycle11 survivor, for prospective cycle12. Preserve all469 calibrated inputs and five fixed RGB formulas. Run/review/select every cycle through20, then complete final all5-conversion benchmark.
